Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replay consumer distribution gate

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

This gate builds the actual Nix addon recipe from a frozen, bounded source snapshot and installs its output into a temporary Godot project outside the repository. It does not modify the shared Git index, create a release branch/tag, or publish an artifact. The snapshot includes current untracked Replay implementation files that a normal Git-flake build would otherwise omit.

Shell
REPLAY_DISTRIBUTION_OUT=/tmp/replay-consumer-check \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_distribution/run.sh

Use a fresh output path. snapshot.py includes only known addon build inputs and the documented consumer files, excluding caches, binaries, game projects and result archives. It writes a source-content manifest before Nix reads the snapshot.

The test copies template/replay/ into the external project, builds using the installed addon's helper with SKIP_CORE=1, and unsets ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL. The prebuilt core must discover the consumer's compiled scripts in the split layout. The starter runs offline and in separate host/client/observer processes, with a conserved shared coin and a remote accepted action. The same packaged web helper builds an actual browser export; Chrome executes the offline starter and captures a screenshot. A WASM type-check is additional evidence, not a replacement for that browser run.

The gate verifies every packaged Replay source against its snapshot, checks source directories' .gdignore files, and rejects original-checkout paths in consumer Odin sources. The source repository is used only by the external test driver/reporting, not by the consumer's collection or build helper. Logs and the temporary consumer remain available for review.

The separate #release package adds cross-built Linux/Windows cores and ZIP/checksum assembly. Runtime acceptance in this environment covers macOS and Chrome; cross-built core formats alone do not establish Linux/Windows runtime support. See recorded evidence.
